question: Which communication method does NFS use for requests between servers and clients?
theory: NFS is built on Sun's Remote Procedure Call (RPC) framework: when a client wants to perform an operation on a remote file, it issues an RPC call to the NFS server, which executes the request and returns a result code (and data, if applicable) over whatever transport RPC is running on (TCP in modern NFS versions). This RPC-based, request/response model is fundamental to how NFS clients and servers communicate, distinguishing it from protocols like SMB that use their own dedicated messaging format. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 10 - NFS Concepts)
